subject: history_social
passage: Across the twentieth century, average scores on intelligence tests rose in country after country by roughly three points per decade, a pattern so steady that test makers periodically had to make their tests harder. Psychologist Dmitri Volkov holds that the best explanation is biological: better nutrition, fewer childhood infections, and smaller families allowed brains to develop more fully than in earlier generations. He notes that the gains were largest in countries where diets improved most dramatically.
passage_b: Nutrition cannot carry the whole explanation. In wealthy countries, improvements in diet had largely leveled off by the middle of the century, yet scores kept climbing for decades afterward. More telling is the shape of the gains. They were smallest on tests of vocabulary and arithmetic, exactly the areas in which better-fed children should also have improved, and largest on tests of abstract pattern-finding, the kind of thinking that extended schooling and modern work demand. The century did not merely feed people better; it trained them to think in the way the tests reward.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation offered by Volkov in Text 1?

choices.A: By claiming that nutrition played no role in rising scores anywhere
choices.B: By denying that scores on intelligence tests rose during the twentieth century
choices.C: By arguing that the pattern of gains across kinds of tests fits schooling better than nutrition
choices.D: By suggesting that scores rose fastest on tests of vocabulary and arithmetic

explanation.why: Volkov explains rising scores through nutrition and health. Text 2 says nutrition "cannot carry the whole explanation," because gains continued after diets leveled off and, "more telling," were smallest in vocabulary and arithmetic and largest in abstract pattern-finding, "the kind of thinking that extended schooling and modern work demand." So the author of Text 2 would respond that the profile of the gains points to training rather than biology.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says nutrition cannot be "the whole explanation," which leaves it some role.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 accepts that scores "kept climbing for decades."
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 argues that the uneven pattern of gains, concentrated in abstract reasoning, is better explained by schooling and modern work than by diet.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says gains were "smallest" on vocabulary and arithmetic.
